title: How To Begin 2021 On The Right Classroom Management Foot
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that reviewing the classroom management plan on the first day back from any holiday break is a small, ten-minute act with outsized impact, since even a two-week gap feels like an eternity to students and erodes established habits. He identifies four benefits: it reestablishes behavior standards as the top priority before academics resume, reminds students they can trust the teacher to protect their right to a peaceful classroom, offers a symbolic fresh start tied to the new year, and sharpens the teacher's own clarity about what does and doesn't count as a rule violation. He frames skipping this step as a costly mistake that leads to a chaotic morning and a stressed, reactive day, urging teachers to be 'bold, clear, unmistakable and unapologetic' the moment students settle into their seats.
points: A two-week break is described as feeling like an eternity to students under eighteen, causing real erosion of established habits.
Reviewing the classroom management plan before any academic content reestablishes behavior standards as the top priority.
The review reminds students they can trust the teacher, letting them relax and focus fully on the day's work.
A first-day-back review offers students a symbolic fresh start tied to the dawn of a new year.
Skipping the review is framed as a costly mistake likely to produce a chaotic, stressful day the teacher then has to fight to recover from.
quotes: Whether you’re teaching in person, online, or a hybrid of the two, there is one thing you must do to begin 2021.
It may not seem like it in your world—especially given how much you cherish your time off—but for anyone under eighteen a two-week holiday feels like an eternity.
By reviewing your classroom management plan on the first day back from break you’re communicating its supreme importance.
Jumping straight into your plan reminds students that they can place their trust in you. They can let down their guard, exhale fully, and focus on enjoying school.
It clears the deck, absolves the lost and fallen, and encourages a turn of a new page and hope for a better tomorrow.
Therefore, as soon as your students settle into their seats, don’t waste a second. Do it now. Be bold. Be clear. Be unmistakable and unapologetic.
